newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SE Asian corn dip on thin demand ahead of holidays.
newsitem.headline: SE Asian corn dip on thin demand ahead of holidays.

text.p: Asian corn prices were a shade softer on Thursday with buyers sidelined as the market paused for the Lunar New Year and the Moslem Eid-ul-Fitri holidays, industry sources said.
The Lunar New Year and Moslem festivities begin February 6 and last until February 10 in most Asian countries.
Traders also said they do not expect any large movement in regional grains and oilseeds prices after the festive season.
"The region has purchased enough corn to tide it over the holidays," the trader said.
U.S. corn coming into Southeast Asia was quoted at around $140-$143 a tonne C&F for April/May delivery on board a Panamax vessel against $145-$155 last week.
"Corn buyers are very cautious with most traders sitting tight waiting for the crop in Thailand and Indonesia to develop and sales to start in the market in March or April," said the trader.
"(Soymeal) market discussions were very thin ahead of the holidays," said a trader with a European firm.
Soymeal traders were taking a relaxed stance with the market focus on the weather in South America and the how the crop is developing.
"There is some Indian soymeal being offered in the market but there were no takers," said one trader.
"The market would be stagnant during the festive season and we would be more certain of market direction after everybody returns mid next week," he said.
GRAINS/OILSEEDS IMPORT PRICES IN SOUTHEAST ASIA:
U.S Corn (March/April) C&F a tonne US$140-143 $145-155
Note: U.S. corn, soybeans and soymeal shipped in a panamax vessel. Indian soymeal in a Tweendecker vessel
